title: 1 Samuel 14: By Many or by Few
body:
Read the chapter → [1 Samuel 14](/bible/1-samuel/14)

**[1 Samuel 14:1-3](/bible/1-samuel/14#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/1-samuel/14#v1)</sup> Now it came to pass upon a day, that Jonathan the son of Saul said unto the young man that bare his armour, Come, and let us go over to the Philistines’ garrison, that is on the other side. But he told not his father.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/1-samuel/14#v2)</sup> And Saul tarried in the uttermost part of Gibeah under a pomegranate tree which is in Migron: and the people that were with him were about six hundred men;
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/1-samuel/14#v3)</sup> And Ahiah, the son of Ahitub, I–chabod’s brother, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli, the Lord’s priest in Shiloh, wearing an ephod. And the people knew not that Jonathan was gone.

- Jonathan said unto the young man that bare his armor, Come, let us go over to the Philistines' garrison on the other side; but he told not his father. Saul tarried under a pomegranate tree in Migron with about six hundred men, with Ahiah the priest wearing an ephod, and the people knew not that Jonathan was gone.

**[1 Samuel 14:4-6](/bible/1-samuel/14#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/1-samuel/14#v4)</sup> And between the passages, by which Jonathan sought to go over unto the Philistines’ garrison, there was a sharp rock on the one side, and a sharp rock on the other side: and the name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other Seneh.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/1-samuel/14#v5)</sup> The forefront of the one was situate northward over against Michmash, and the other southward over against Gibeah.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/1-samuel/14#v6)</sup> And Jonathan said to the young man that bare his armour, Come, and let us go over unto the garrison of these uncircumcised: it may be that the Lord will work for us: for there is no restraint to the Lord to save by many or by few.

- Between the passages were two sharp rocks, Bozez and Seneh, one facing Michmash and the other Gibeah. Jonathan said, Come, let us go over unto the garrison of these uncircumcised; it may be that the Lord will work for us: for there is no restraint to the Lord to save by many or by few.
- The Lord put that spirit on Jonathan. That is how the Most High operates: he loves to show his power by having a small number defeat a very large number. That is why it will be the 144,000 taking over the whole world; that is just how he rolls.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 Maccabees 3:18-19](/bible/1-maccabees/3#v18)**
    > <sup>[18](/bible/1-maccabees/3#v18)</sup> Unto whom Judas answered, It is no hard matter for many to be shut up in the hands of a few; and with the God of heaven it is all one, to deliver with a great multitude, or a small company:
    >
    > <sup>[19](/bible/1-maccabees/3#v19)</sup> For the victory of battle standeth not in the multitude of an host; but strength cometh from heaven.

    Judas answered, It is no hard matter for many to be shut up in the hands of a few; and with the God of heaven it is all one to deliver with a great multitude or a small company; we do not have to come deep to get the victory.
  - **[2 Chronicles 14:11](/bible/2-chronicles/14#v11)**
    > <sup>[11](/bible/2-chronicles/14#v11)</sup> And Asa cried unto the Lord his God, and said, Lord, it is nothing with thee to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power: help us, O Lord our God; for we rest on thee, and in thy name we go against this multitude. O Lord, thou art our God; let not man prevail against thee.

    Asa cried unto the Lord, It is nothing with thee to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power: help us, O Lord our God, for we rest on thee, and in thy name we go against this multitude; that is the faith you see in Jonathan and this young servant, two men going against an army in the name of the Lord.

**[1 Samuel 14:7-10](/bible/1-samuel/14#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/1-samuel/14#v7)</sup> And his armourbearer said unto him, Do all that is in thine heart: turn thee; behold, I am with thee according to thy heart.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/1-samuel/14#v8)</sup> Then said Jonathan, Behold, we will pass over unto these men, and we will discover ourselves unto them.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/1-samuel/14#v9)</sup> If they say thus unto us, Tarry until we come to you; then we will stand still in our place, and will not go up unto them.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/1-samuel/14#v10)</sup> But if they say thus, Come up unto us; then we will go up: for the Lord hath delivered them into our hand: and this shall be a sign unto us.

- His armor bearer said, Do all that is in thine heart: behold, I am with thee according to thy heart. Jonathan set the sign: we will discover ourselves unto them; if they say, Tarry until we come to you, we will stand still in our place; but if they say, Come up unto us, then we will go up, for the Lord hath delivered them into our hand. That is how they would know the Lord had given the green light.

**[1 Samuel 14:11-14](/bible/1-samuel/14#v11)**

> <sup>[11](/bible/1-samuel/14#v11)</sup> And both of them discovered themselves unto the garrison of the Philistines: and the Philistines said, Behold, the Hebrews come forth out of the holes where they had hid themselves.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/1-samuel/14#v12)</sup> And the men of the garrison answered Jonathan and his armourbearer, and said, Come up to us, and we will shew you a thing. And Jonathan said unto his armourbearer, Come up after me: for the Lord hath delivered them into the hand of Israel.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/1-samuel/14#v13)</sup> And Jonathan climbed up upon his hands and upon his feet, and his armourbearer after him: and they fell before Jonathan; and his armourbearer slew after him.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/1-samuel/14#v14)</sup> And that first slaughter, which Jonathan and his armourbearer made, was about twenty men, within as it were an half acre of land, which a yoke of oxen might plow.

- Both of them showed themselves to the garrison, and the Philistines said, Behold, the Hebrews come forth out of the holes where they had hid themselves; and the men of the garrison said, Come up to us, and we will shew you a thing. The sign came to pass exactly; the Lord had delivered them into the hand of Israel.
- Jonathan climbed up upon his hands and upon his feet, his armor bearer after him, and that first slaughter was about twenty men within about half an acre of land. Two men against a garrison.
- Some hold a doctrine that Jonathan was a homosexual; this act answers it. Scaling a rock face to rush a garrison two-deep is a bold, manly act of war that most men are not cut out for; he carried himself like a real man.

**[1 Samuel 14:15-16](/bible/1-samuel/14#v15)**

> <sup>[15](/bible/1-samuel/14#v15)</sup> And there was trembling in the host, in the field, and among all the people: the garrison, and the spoilers, they also trembled, and the earth quaked: so it was a very great trembling.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/1-samuel/14#v16)</sup> And the watchmen of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin looked; and, behold, the multitude melted away, and they went on beating down one another.

- There was trembling in the host, in the field, and among all the people; the garrison and the spoilers also trembled, and the earth quaked, so it was a very great trembling. The Philistines got caught off guard and panicked.
- The watchmen of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin looked, and behold, the multitude melted away, and they went on beating down one another; in their panic and confusion the Philistines started beating on each other.

**[1 Samuel 14:17-23](/bible/1-samuel/14#v17)**

> <sup>[17](/bible/1-samuel/14#v17)</sup> Then said Saul unto the people that were with him, Number now, and see who is gone from us. And when they had numbered, behold, Jonathan and his armourbearer were not there.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/1-samuel/14#v18)</sup> And Saul said unto Ahiah, Bring hither the ark of God. For the ark of God was at that time with the children of Israel.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/1-samuel/14#v19)</sup> And it came to pass, while Saul talked unto the priest, that the noise that was in the host of the Philistines went on and increased: and Saul said unto the priest, Withdraw thine hand.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/1-samuel/14#v20)</sup> And Saul and all the people that were with him assembled themselves, and they came to the battle: and, behold, every man’s sword was against his fellow, and there was a very great discomfiture.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/1-samuel/14#v21)</sup> Moreover the Hebrews that were with the Philistines before that time, which went up with them into the camp from the country round about, even they also turned to be with the Israelites that were with Saul and Jonathan.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/1-samuel/14#v22)</sup> Likewise all the men of Israel which had hid themselves in mount Ephraim, when they heard that the Philistines fled, even they also followed hard after them in the battle.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/1-samuel/14#v23)</sup> So the Lord saved Israel that day: and the battle passed over unto Beth–aven.

- Saul numbered the people and found Jonathan and his armor bearer missing. While Saul talked with the priest, the noise in the host of the Philistines went on and increased, and when Israel came to the battle, behold, every man's sword was against his fellow, and there was a very great discomfiture; the enemies were destroying each other, and Israel did not have to put in the work.
- The Hebrews that were with the Philistines from the country round about turned to be with the Israelites that were with Saul and Jonathan, and the men of Israel which had hid themselves in mount Ephraim followed hard after them in the battle when they heard the Philistines fled.
- So the Lord saved Israel that day, and the battle passed over unto Bethaven.

**[1 Samuel 14:24-26](/bible/1-samuel/14#v24)**

> <sup>[24](/bible/1-samuel/14#v24)</sup> And the men of Israel were distressed that day: for Saul had adjured the people, saying, Cursed be the man that eateth any food until evening, that I may be avenged on mine enemies. So none of the people tasted any food.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/1-samuel/14#v25)</sup> And all they of the land came to a wood; and there was honey upon the ground.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/1-samuel/14#v26)</sup> And when the people were come into the wood, behold, the honey dropped; but no man put his hand to his mouth: for the people feared the oath.

- Saul had adjured the people, saying, Cursed be the man that eateth any food until evening, that I may be avenged on mine enemies; so none of the people tasted any food. Saul put out a strange order, and the men of Israel were distressed that day.
- All they of the land came to a wood, and there was honey upon the ground, and the honey dropped, but no man put his hand to his mouth, for the people feared the oath.
- But Jonathan heard not when his father charged the people with the oath; he was not there when the order came out.

**[1 Samuel 14:27-30](/bible/1-samuel/14#v27)**

> <sup>[27](/bible/1-samuel/14#v27)</sup> But Jonathan heard not when his father charged the people with the oath: wherefore he put forth the end of the rod that was in his hand, and dipped it in an honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes were enlightened.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/1-samuel/14#v28)</sup> Then answered one of the people, and said, Thy father straitly charged the people with an oath, saying, Cursed be the man that eateth any food this day. And the people were faint.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/1-samuel/14#v29)</sup> Then said Jonathan, My father hath troubled the land: see, I pray you, how mine eyes have been enlightened, because I tasted a little of this honey.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/1-samuel/14#v30)</sup> How much more, if haply the people had eaten freely to day of the spoil of their enemies which they found? for had there not been now a much greater slaughter among the Philistines?

- Jonathan dipped the end of his rod in an honeycomb and put his hand to his mouth, and his eyes were enlightened; like the first taste after a long fast, he felt like a whole new creature. Then one of the people told him his father straitly charged the people with an oath, and the people were faint.
- Jonathan said, My father hath troubled the land: see how mine eyes have been enlightened, because I tasted a little of this honey; how much more, if haply the people had eaten freely of the spoil of their enemies, had there not been now a much greater slaughter among the Philistines? He began to convince the people that eating was the better idea and that the king's order was folly.

  Precepts:
  - **[Proverbs 24:21](/bible/proverbs/24#v21)**
    > <sup>[21](/bible/proverbs/24#v21)</sup> My son, fear thou the Lord and the king: and meddle not with them that are given to change:

    My son, fear thou the Lord and the king, and meddle not with them that are given to change; Saul was the king and put out an order, and when someone among you tries to change the orders of the king, do not meddle with him, because he will lead you into error, which is exactly what happened next.

**[1 Samuel 14:31-35](/bible/1-samuel/14#v31)**

> <sup>[31](/bible/1-samuel/14#v31)</sup> And they smote the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon: and the people were very faint.
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/1-samuel/14#v32)</sup> And the people flew upon the spoil, and took sheep, and oxen, and calves, and slew them on the ground: and the people did eat them with the blood.
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/1-samuel/14#v33)</sup> Then they told Saul, saying, Behold, the people sin against the Lord, in that they eat with the blood. And he said, Ye have transgressed: roll a great stone unto me this day.
>
> <sup>[34](/bible/1-samuel/14#v34)</sup> And Saul said, Disperse yourselves among the people, and say unto them, Bring me hither every man his ox, and every man his sheep, and slay them here, and eat; and sin not against the Lord in eating with the blood. And all the people brought every man his ox with him that night, and slew them there.
>
> <sup>[35](/bible/1-samuel/14#v35)</sup> And Saul built an altar unto the Lord: the same was the first altar that he built unto the Lord.

- They smote the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon, and the people were very faint. Then the people flew upon the spoil, took sheep, oxen, and calves, slew them on the ground, and did eat them with the blood; too faint to prepare the meat, they ate it raw with the blood, and that was the transgression Jonathan's talk led the people into.
- When they told Saul, he said, Ye have transgressed: roll a great stone unto me this day; bring every man his ox and his sheep, slay them here, and eat, and sin not against the Lord in eating with the blood. And Saul built an altar unto the Lord, the first altar that he built unto the Lord.

**[1 Samuel 14:36-37](/bible/1-samuel/14#v36)**

> <sup>[36](/bible/1-samuel/14#v36)</sup> And Saul said, Let us go down after the Philistines by night, and spoil them until the morning light, and let us not leave a man of them. And they said, Do whatsoever seemeth good unto thee. Then said the priest, Let us draw near hither unto God.
>
> <sup>[37](/bible/1-samuel/14#v37)</sup> And Saul asked counsel of God, Shall I go down after the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into the hand of Israel? But he answered him not that day.

- Saul proposed going down after the Philistines by night to spoil them until morning, and the people agreed; then said the priest, Let us draw near hither unto God. And Saul asked counsel of God, Shall I go down after the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into the hand of Israel? But he answered him not that day.
- If you are spiritual, when the Lord ignores you, you understand at that point what it reveals: it is sin. It has to be; the scriptures give only that reason.

  Precepts:
  - **[Psalms 66:18](/bible/psalms/66#v18)**
    > <sup>[18](/bible/psalms/66#v18)</sup> If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me:

    If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me; somewhere in the camp there was iniquity, so the Lord did not hear Saul.
  - **[Isaiah 59:2](/bible/isaiah/59#v2)**
    > <sup>[2](/bible/isaiah/59#v2)</sup> But your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear.

    Your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear; sin and iniquity are what cause the Most High not to hear you, plain and clear.

**[1 Samuel 14:38-44](/bible/1-samuel/14#v38)**

> <sup>[38](/bible/1-samuel/14#v38)</sup> And Saul said, Draw ye near hither, all the chief of the people: and know and see wherein this sin hath been this day.
>
> <sup>[39](/bible/1-samuel/14#v39)</sup> For, as the Lord liveth, which saveth Israel, though it be in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die. But there was not a man among all the people that answered him.
>
> <sup>[40](/bible/1-samuel/14#v40)</sup> Then said he unto all Israel, Be ye on one side, and I and Jonathan my son will be on the other side. And the people said unto Saul, Do what seemeth good unto thee.
>
> <sup>[41](/bible/1-samuel/14#v41)</sup> Therefore Saul said unto the Lord God of Israel, Give a perfect lot. And Saul and Jonathan were taken: but the people escaped.
>
> <sup>[42](/bible/1-samuel/14#v42)</sup> And Saul said, Cast lots between me and Jonathan my son. And Jonathan was taken.
>
> <sup>[43](/bible/1-samuel/14#v43)</sup> Then Saul said to Jonathan, Tell me what thou hast done. And Jonathan told him, and said, I did but taste a little honey with the end of the rod that was in mine hand, and, lo, I must die.
>
> <sup>[44](/bible/1-samuel/14#v44)</sup> And Saul answered, God do so and more also: for thou shalt surely die, Jonathan.

- Saul said, Draw ye near, all the chief of the people, and know and see wherein this sin hath been this day; for as the Lord liveth, which saveth Israel, though it be in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die. But there was not a man among all the people that answered him.
- Saul said unto the Lord God of Israel, Give a perfect lot; and Saul and Jonathan were taken, but the people escaped. Then they cast lots between Saul and Jonathan, and Jonathan was taken.
- Jonathan told him, I did but taste a little honey with the end of the rod that was in mine hand, and, lo, I must die. And Saul answered, God do so and more also: for thou shalt surely die, Jonathan. Saul was ready to kill his own son over the oath.

**[1 Samuel 14:45](/bible/1-samuel/14#v45)**

> <sup>[45](/bible/1-samuel/14#v45)</sup> And the people said unto Saul, Shall Jonathan die, who hath wrought this great salvation in Israel? God forbid: as the Lord liveth, there shall not one hair of his head fall to the ground; for he hath wrought with God this day. So the people rescued Jonathan, that he died not.

- The people said unto Saul, Shall Jonathan die, who hath wrought this great salvation in Israel? God forbid: as the Lord liveth, there shall not one hair of his head fall to the ground, for he hath wrought with God this day. So the people rescued Jonathan, that he died not; they kept him from the wrath of his father.
- Think about the contrast, and why the scripture says to get the love of the congregation. In chapter 13 Saul was the one disobeying the voice of the Lord and getting rebuked, while Jonathan was brave and mighty and had just saved Israel out of the hand of its enemies; now the coward wants to kill the deliverer.
- In some situations you have to weigh it like the people did: yes, he made a mistake and crossed the order, but he just saved all our lives.

  Precepts:
  - **[James 2:13](/bible/james/2#v13)**
    > <sup>[13](/bible/james/2#v13)</sup> For he shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy; and mercy rejoiceth against judgment.

    He shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy, and mercy rejoiceth against judgment; Saul had just been shown mercy for his own failure, so passing merciless judgment on his own son would have left no mercy for Saul the next time he fell.

**[1 Samuel 14:47-52](/bible/1-samuel/14#v47)**

> <sup>[47](/bible/1-samuel/14#v47)</sup> So Saul took the kingdom over Israel, and fought against all his enemies on every side, against Moab, and against the children of Ammon, and against Edom, and against the kings of Zobah, and against the Philistines: and whithersoever he turned himself, he vexed them.
>
> <sup>[48](/bible/1-samuel/14#v48)</sup> And he gathered an host, and smote the Amalekites, and delivered Israel out of the hands of them that spoiled them.
>
> <sup>[49](/bible/1-samuel/14#v49)</sup> Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, and Ishui, and Melchi–shua: and the names of his two daughters were these; the name of the firstborn Merab, and the name of the younger Michal:
>
> <sup>[50](/bible/1-samuel/14#v50)</sup> And the name of Saul’s wife was Ahinoam, the daughter of Ahimaaz: and the name of the captain of his host was Abner, the son of Ner, Saul’s uncle.
>
> <sup>[51](/bible/1-samuel/14#v51)</sup> And Kish was the father of Saul; and Ner the father of Abner was the son of Abiel.
>
> <sup>[52](/bible/1-samuel/14#v52)</sup> And there was sore war against the Philistines all the days of Saul: and when Saul saw any strong man, or any valiant man, he took him unto him.

- Saul took the kingdom over Israel and fought against all his enemies on every side: Moab, the children of Ammon, Edom, the kings of Zobah, and the Philistines; and whithersoever he turned himself, he vexed them. He gathered an host, smote the Amalekites, and delivered Israel out of the hands of them that spoiled them.
- The chapter closes with his house: his sons Jonathan, Ishui, and Melchishua; his daughters Merab and Michal, whom we will learn about later; his wife Ahinoam; and Abner the son of Ner, Saul's uncle, captain of his host. There was sore war against the Philistines all the days of Saul, and when Saul saw any strong man or any valiant man, he took him unto him.
